messages:
From: Naomi Feldman <naomi@redwood.com>
To: Tom Briggs <t.briggs@humacare.com>, HumaCare Onboarding <onboarding@humacare.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>, Jasmine Liu <jasmine@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 10 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Edge Enclave access & certification plan

Tom / HumaCare team —

Thanks again for the kickoff yesterday. Per our conversation I put together a concise checklist to get the private deployment "edge enclave" certified and reachable from your environment. Goal: make day‑0 ops minimal and have all access/evidence we need for the certification audit. Key asks below; attached are the enclave topology PDF and a starter access matrix.

Priority checklist (what we need from HumaCare before we schedule the handoff run):
- Control plane reachability: confirm your firewall ACLs allow TCP 443 and 50051 from Redwood control plane IPs (listed in the access_matrix spreadsheet).
- Private peering: confirm whether you prefer VPC peering (AWS) vs. Transit Gateway; include the account IDs and desired AZs.
- Egress policy: final egress CIDR list for model telemetry and updates (we need static outbound ranges for NAT).
- KMS: provide the KMS ARN you want Redwood to wrap with; list key policy owners. We will need a cross-account grant or a managed key role. See kms_key_policy_snippet.txt.
- MTU and overlay: confirm if your network drops jumbo frames; recommended MTU 1500 for our tunneling.
- Calico/CNI constraints: any namespace-level network policies that could block health checks on port 8080/9090 (health/metrics).
- Admin access: list of up to 3 operator emails for initial SSH/Jumpbox access and whether you require bastion session recording.

Operational notes:
- We will ship a small smoke image that performs a signed health handshake; expect a 10–15 minute maintenance window for the initial bootstrap.
- Attachments: enclave_topology_v1.pdf (diagram), access_matrix_humacare.xlsx (ACL / IP list template), kms_key_policy_snippet.txt (example).

Please confirm the items you can provide this week and flag any blockers. If you prefer, Marcus can run a 30‑minute technical call to walk the topology and the required IAM changes.

Thanks,
Naomi Feldman
Senior Technical Program Manager
Redwood Inference

Appreciate the clear list. Quick answers from our side: we can provide the egress CIDRs and account IDs by Thursday 11/12. We prefer Transit Gateway for peering (will share TGW attachment IDs).

A few clarifying items:

Thanks Tom — Thu 11/12 10:00am PT works for us. Agenda for the 30‑minute technical call:
1) Walk topology (enclave_topology_v1.pdf) and peering options (TGW vs peering).
2) IAM/KMS grant flow (I will share a minimal CloudFormation snippet during the call).
3) Network health checks and required ports: inbound 443 (control plane), 50051 (gRPC), 8080/9090 (local metrics/health).
4) Egress CIDR confirmation and NAT behavior (our runtime pulls container updates / telemetry to these endpoints).
5) Post‑install test plan (smoke test steps + success criteria).

Action items we will complete before the call:
- I will upload a short CloudFormation snippet to the Confluence card and paste the link in the invite.
- Jasmine will prepare the initial access matrix prefilled with Redwood control plane IPs.

If session recording for bastion is a hard requirement we can enable it — note that auditing logs will be saved to the HumaCare S3/CloudTrail you provide.

See you on the call.

Marcus Lin
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
